{
  "technical_and_design_decisions": [
    "Use the existing Spring XD module, configuration, job lifecycle, and documentation conventions rather than introducing new framework abstractions where possible.",
    "Represent Hadoop namenode settings through an application or DSL-session configuration property with sensible validation and precedence over explicitly supplied session values.",
    "Implement jdbchdfs passthrough as an explicit non-chunking execution mode that transfers data without invoking batch reader, processor, and writer chunk overhead.",
    "Decouple execution context creation and persistence from job launch lifecycle using the Spring Batch-compatible execution-context behavior, then remove or refactor the existing XD-2486 workaround.",
    "Support custom Java-configured jobs by discovering and registering job beans from uploaded modules consistently with existing XML job deployment and launch semantics.",
    "Define the Lattice/Diego integration around a provider-neutral execution SPI, with the Receptor API implemented as an adapter rather than embedding Receptor-specific behavior in core XD code.",
    "Expose shortDescription as module metadata and render it consistently in generated and existing module documentation.",
    "Implement HDFS-backed Python script resolution in the shell processor, downloading or streaming the script to the execution environment before invoking the configured Python runtime.",
    "Use automated unit and integration tests for configuration, job lifecycle, module deployment, HDFS access, SPI behavior, and backward compatibility."
  ],
  "assumptions": [
    "The estimate covers one software developer's work in work-hours and includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, documentation updates, and local integration verification.",
    "The existing Spring XD and Spring Batch codebase, build system, test infrastructure, and supported Hadoop/HDFS clients are available and build successfully before the increment starts.",
    "No major upgrade of Java, Spring Framework, Spring Batch, Hadoop, or the deployment platform is required beyond the dependency changes directly needed for these stories.",
    "For U1, the wiki consists of repository-compatible Markdown or similar static documentation; no new documentation hosting system is required.",
    "For U2, namenode configuration is local to the XD installation or DSL session and does not require a new administrative UI or remote configuration service.",
    "For U3, jdbchdfs already has working normal batch read/write behavior; the increment adds a passthrough option rather than redesigning the module.",
    "For U4, the required Spring Batch change can be implemented or consumed within the project dependency workflow without waiting for an external release or coordinating with an external team.",
    "For U5, uploaded custom job modules can be loaded using the existing module class-loading and deployment mechanisms; no general-purpose plugin isolation redesign is required.",
    "For U6, the deliverable is a functional provider-neutral SPI and a Receptor-oriented implementation suitable for the PoC, not a production-grade Diego deployment, high availability design, or complete platform certification.",
    "For U7, module documentation can be updated from existing metadata and templates; no new documentation authoring workflow is required.",
    "For U8, HDFS authentication and network connectivity are already supported by the deployment environment, and the Python runtime is installed and accessible on the target execution host.",
    "Security hardening, performance benchmarking at production scale, migration of unrelated legacy defects, and elapsed time for external reviews or releases are excluded."
  ],
  "activities": [
    {
      "activity_id": "A1",
      "activity_name": "Increment analysis and technical design",
      "activity_description": "Inspect the existing XD, Spring Batch, module, documentation, HDFS, and deployment architecture; trace affected code paths; define interfaces, configuration behavior, compatibility constraints, and implementation sequencing for U1-U8.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A2",
      "activity_name": "Migrate wiki content into the project repository",
      "activity_description": "Collect and normalize wiki pages, convert them to repository documentation format, preserve navigation and links where practical, add repository contribution guidance, and verify generated or rendered documentation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 16
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A3",
      "activity_name": "Add configurable Hadoop namenode settings",
      "activity_description": "Add configuration properties and defaults for namenode location, integrate them with DSL session initialization, define precedence and validation behavior, update configuration documentation, and add unit and session-level tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A4",
      "activity_name": "Implement jdbchdfs passthrough batch mode",
      "activity_description": "Add the passthrough execution path and configuration, bypass chunk processing while preserving required transfer semantics, handle errors and lifecycle behavior, and add tests covering normal and passthrough modes.",
      "most_likely_effort": 40
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A5",
      "activity_name": "Decouple execution context from job launch lifecycle",
      "activity_description": "Modify the Spring Batch/XD job execution-context handling, apply the compatible Spring Batch change or dependency update, refactor the XD-2486 workaround, address class-loader and serialization boundaries, and add regression tests for launch, restart, and serialization scenarios.",
      "most_likely_effort": 80
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A6",
      "activity_name": "Support Java Config custom job modules",
      "activity_description": "Extend uploaded job-module discovery and registration to recognize Java-configured job definitions, ensure deployed jobs become launchable through the existing CLI and lifecycle, diagnose class-loader or bean registration issues, and add deployment and launch integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 56
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A7",
      "activity_name": "Design and implement pluggable Lattice/Diego execution SPI",
      "activity_description": "Define the provider-neutral execution and lifecycle interfaces, implement the Receptor API adapter, connect the SPI to the XD PoC execution flow, handle status and error propagation, and add mock-provider and adapter integration tests.",
      "most_likely_effort": 120
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A8",
      "activity_name": "Add shortDescription to module documentation",
      "activity_description": "Extend module metadata extraction, templates, and documentation generation to include shortDescription; update existing module documentation and add validation or snapshot tests for the generated output.",
      "most_likely_effort": 32
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A9",
      "activity_name": "Support Python scripts hosted in HDFS",
      "activity_description": "Add HDFS URI handling to the shell processor, retrieve or stage the Python script for execution, preserve arguments and output handling, implement cleanup and failure behavior, document configuration, and test local and HDFS-backed scripts.",
      "most_likely_effort": 80
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A10",
      "activity_name": "Cross-feature integration, regression testing, and defect resolution",
      "activity_description": "Run the complete build and relevant integration suites, test interactions among configuration, module deployment, job launching, execution contexts, HDFS access, and platform adapters, fix defects, and verify backward compatibility.",
      "most_likely_effort": 80
    },
    {
      "activity_id": "A11",
      "activity_name": "Release preparation and final documentation",
      "activity_description": "Update release notes and configuration references, finalize migration and operational guidance, clean up build and dependency metadata, and prepare the increment for repository integration and release validation.",
      "most_likely_effort": 24
    }
  ],
  "reported_total": {
    "most_likely_effort": 576
  }
}

technical_and_design_decisions: Use the existing Spring XD module, configuration, job lifecycle, and documentation conventions rather than introducing new framework abstractions where possible.
Represent Hadoop namenode settings through an application or DSL-session configuration property with sensible validation and precedence over explicitly supplied session values.
Implement jdbchdfs passthrough as an explicit non-chunking execution mode that transfers data without invoking batch reader, processor, and writer chunk overhead.
Decouple execution context creation and persistence from job launch lifecycle using the Spring Batch-compatible execution-context behavior, then remove or refactor the existing XD-2486 workaround.
Support custom Java-configured jobs by discovering and registering job beans from uploaded modules consistently with existing XML job deployment and launch semantics.
Define the Lattice/Diego integration around a provider-neutral execution SPI, with the Receptor API implemented as an adapter rather than embedding Receptor-specific behavior in core XD code.
Expose shortDescription as module metadata and render it consistently in generated and existing module documentation.
Implement HDFS-backed Python script resolution in the shell processor, downloading or streaming the script to the execution environment before invoking the configured Python runtime.
Use automated unit and integration tests for configuration, job lifecycle, module deployment, HDFS access, SPI behavior, and backward compatibility.
assumptions: The estimate covers one software developer's work in work-hours and includes implementation, code review preparation, automated tests, documentation updates, and local integration verification.
The existing Spring XD and Spring Batch codebase, build system, test infrastructure, and supported Hadoop/HDFS clients are available and build successfully before the increment starts.
No major upgrade of Java, Spring Framework, Spring Batch, Hadoop, or the deployment platform is required beyond the dependency changes directly needed for these stories.
For U1, the wiki consists of repository-compatible Markdown or similar static documentation; no new documentation hosting system is required.
For U2, namenode configuration is local to the XD installation or DSL session and does not require a new administrative UI or remote configuration service.
For U3, jdbchdfs already has working normal batch read/write behavior; the increment adds a passthrough option rather than redesigning the module.
For U4, the required Spring Batch change can be implemented or consumed within the project dependency workflow without waiting for an external release or coordinating with an external team.
For U5, uploaded custom job modules can be loaded using the existing module class-loading and deployment mechanisms; no general-purpose plugin isolation redesign is required.

For U6, the deliverable is a functional provider-neutral SPI and a Receptor-oriented implementation suitable for the PoC, not a production-grade Diego deployment, high availability design, or complete platform certification.
For U7, module documentation can be updated from existing metadata and templates; no new documentation authoring workflow is required.
For U8, HDFS authentication and network connectivity are already supported by the deployment environment, and the Python runtime is installed and accessible on the target execution host.
Security hardening, performance benchmarking at production scale, migration of unrelated legacy defects, and elapsed time for external reviews or releases are excluded.
